args.name: Sela Thorn

properties.role: Tide-reader and boatwoman at pier four; the only one who rows near the bell water
properties.played_as: Whispers as if the water might hear her; never meets anyone's eye, keeps her gaze on the tide line. Grey braid, salt-stained coat, mends a net on an upturned skiff.
properties.knows: Saltmere flooded the night the bell first rang, forty years ago; her grandmother said the water came up warm.

sources.quote: Sela Thorn. I read the tides. I'll row you, but not at night. Never at night.
She talks in a whisper, like the water might hear her, and she never once looks you in the eye.

args.why: New NPC the GM voiced; the party hired her as boatwoman.

args.name: The Tarred Gull

properties.details_shown: Tavern by the docks. Fire going, smells of tar and fish stew.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.

args.why: New place where the party rests.

args.name: Bram

properties.played_as: Huge, red beard, laughs at his own jokes, wipes the same mug the whole time he talks. Friendly to the party; feeds them on the house.
properties.knows: Has known Maren Vosk for thirty years.

sources.quote: Bram is huge, red beard, laughs at his own jokes, and he wipes the same mug the whole time he talks to you.
You lot went to the shore at midnight? Brave or stupid. On the house, either way.

args.why: New NPC the GM voiced.

args.name: Saltmere flooded the night the bell first rang

properties.statement: Saltmere Mine flooded forty years ago on the same night the bell first rang, and the water came up warm.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

args.why: Sela states it; it links the mine to the bell.

args.name: The Kelp Mother

properties.statement: Local fishermen say the Kelp Mother pulls children down by the ankles if they stand too close to the water; whether she is real is unconfirmed.

sources.quote: Don't stand that close. The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.
That's what the fishermen say.

args.why: Local folklore; kept as rumor, not fact.

args.name: Maren Vosk lost a brother to the bay

properties.statement: Maren Vosk lost a brother to the bay.

sources.quote: Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

args.why: Bram's account of Maren's past.

args.name: Is Maren Vosk in the choir?

properties.what_is_open: Vessa and Oren suspect the harbor-master is behind the Hollow Choir. Only the players' guess; nothing at the table supports it yet.

sources.quote: Maren wanted us gone from day one. She's in the cult, I'm calling it.
You can think that.

args.why: Player theory, tracked as a thread only; the GM did not confirm it.

args.name: Dive to the drowned chapel at low tide

properties.what_is_open: The party wants to see where the hymns came from, since Mira wrote in the hymn book.
properties.next_step: Meet Sela at pier four at first light; she rows them out and they dive at low tide, by day only. Vessa buys rope and a second lantern tonight.

sources.quote: So tomorrow, first light, Sela rows us out and we dive to the chapel at low tide. I'll buy rope and a second lantern tonight.
Agreed. Tomorrow we dive.

args.why: The party's stated plan for next session.

properties.details_shown: Up the cliff path, about an hour's walk. A black mouth in the chalk, timber frame half rotted, a rusted cart on its side. Warm air smelling of church and old candle wax. Thirty paces in the tunnel is flooded with warm black water; wet hymn-book pages float on it and cling to the walls.

sources.quote: The air coming out of it is warm and smells like a church, like old candle wax.
About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch.

args.why: The party visited and saw it.

properties.details_shown: Sank into the bay with its bell. At low water the roof, the bell tower and two broken arches stick out, seaweed hanging from the stones. At midnight the bell rings under the water twelve times; pale shapes stand in rows on the chapel floor, like a congregation, then vanish when the bell stops.

sources.quote: The drowned chapel's roof sticks out of the bay at low water, just the bell tower and two broken arches.
Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation.

args.why: The party saw the chapel and the shapes.

sources.quote: (to himself) That's the choir clock at three of six.

args.why: The GM advanced the clock from 2 to 3 of 6 after the louder midnight ringing.

properties.what_changed: A wet hymn-book page in Saltmere Mine has "M. Brand" pencilled in the margin; Teo says it is Mira's handwriting, so she was there. (Teo's identification is not confirmed by the GM.)

sources.quote: A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".
That's Mira. That's my sister's handwriting. She was here.

args.why: New clue for Teo's goal.

properties.details_shown: Fog, tar, and gulls; the far piers are rotting. Pier four is where the party looks for a boat; Sela Thorn mends nets there.

sources.quote: The fog is still sitting on the docks, gulls everywhere, and you're standing at the end of pier four looking for a boat.

args.why: Adds pier four detail.

sources.quote: She says she'll be at pier four tomorrow at first light if you want the ride.

args.why: Where the table last saw Sela.

sources.quote: The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.

args.why: Bram runs the Tarred Gull.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang.

args.why: The fact is about Saltmere.

sources.quote: She lost a brother to that bay.

args.why: The fact is about Maren.

sources.quote: Maren wanted us gone from day one. She's in the cult, I'm calling it.

args.why: The theory is about Maren.

sources.quote: We go down to the chapel.

args.why: The plan targets the chapel.

sources.quote: Sela rows us out and we dive to the chapel at low tide.

args.why: Sela is the boatwoman for the plan.
